podcast.title: Connection to Courtney Love (Post-1994)
podcast.body: The Mentors, an extreme LA punk band, became tangentially involved in the Kurt Cobain death investigation through two of their members. Guitarist Eric Carlson (Sikki Wifebeater) dated Carolyn Rue, who helped Courtney Love found Hole, and it was through this connection that Courtney met singer Elden Hoke (Elduchet). "Carolyn Rue, helped Courtney Love found Hull. She once went out with the guitarist of the mentors, a dude by the name of Eric Carlson, who worked under the name Sikki Wifebeater."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: "Kings of Sleeze" Self-Description
podcast.body: The Mentors, an extreme punk band from Los Angeles, proudly referred to themselves as the "Kings of Sleeze," a moniker that reflected their provocative and controversial image. This self-proclaimed title was frequently associated with their frontman, Elden Hoke (Eldu-Cher). "They proudly refer to themselves as the Kings of Sleeves."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Disassociation by GWAR
podcast.body: Even GWAR, a band known for its extreme antics, wanted nothing to do with The Mentors, indicating their particularly controversial nature. "Even Guar wanted nothing to do with them. That'll give you some idea."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Leader El Ducche's Death and Claims
podcast.body: Their leader, El Ducche, died when he was decapitated by a train, and he controversially claimed that Courtney Love had hired him to kill Kurt Cobain. "And leader El Ducche, he died when he was decapitated by a train. Oh, and he claimed that Courtney Love had hired him to kill Kurt Cobain."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Pornor/Rape Rock Naming
podcast.body: The Mentors, a band from Seattle, alternatively referred to their garage punk metal style as "Pornor Rock" or "Rape Rock." "garage punk metal and what they alternatively called Pornor Rock or rape rock."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Racist Content
podcast.body: The band was known for often incorporating very racist content into their music. "And often very racist, maybe stay away from the mentors."

xref.title: Alleged Murder-for-Hire Offer (1993)
xref.body: Elden Hoke (Elduchet), singer for The Mentors, claimed in the April 1996 edition of High Times Magazine that in December 1993, Courtney Love offered him $50,000 to kill her husband, Kurt Cobain. Hoke quoted her as saying, "I need you to blow my old man's head off. I'll give you $50,000 to blow his effing head off." "Courtney Love offered him $50,000 to kill her husband."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Elden Hoke's Allegations of Murder-for-Hire (December 1993)
xref.body: Elden Hoke (Eldu-Cher), frontman of the punk band The Mentors, publicly claimed in a 1996 High Times interview and a 1998 documentary that Courtney Love offered him $50,000 in December 1993 to kill Kurt Cobain. Hoke stated she said, "I need you to blow my old man's head off." He recounted an exchange outside a Los Angeles record store, corroborated by the owner, and said Courtney later called for him in March 1994. Although Hoke passed a lie detector test, his claims remain unverified and are often dismissed due to his unreliable narrator status. "Eldu-Cher claimed that in December 1993, Courtney offered him $50,000 to kill her husband."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Elden Hoke's Side Project (Post-1994)
xref.body: This band was a side project formed by Elden Hoke (Elduchet), the singer of The Mentors. The band's name itself reflects Hoke's direct accusations against Courtney Love regarding Kurt Cobain's death. "Elle Ducet had a side project to the mentors. The man was called Courtney Killed Kurt."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Role in Hole's Founding and Relationship to The Mentors (Year Unknown)
xref.body: Carolyn Rue played a role in helping Courtney Love found the band Hole. She was also romantically involved with Eric Carlson, known as Sikki Wifebeater, the guitarist of the extreme LA punk band The Mentors, which established a connection between Courtney Love and Elden Hoke. "Carolyn Rue, helped Courtney Love found Hull. She once went out with the guitarist of the mentors, a dude by the name of Eric Carlson, who worked under the name Sikki Wifebeater."
